title: The Complete Guide to Free Hosting for Static Website (2026)
meta_description: What does Free Hosting for Static Website cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives…
intro: Let's be honest: the internet is full of posts that pretend free hosting for static website is complicated. It isn't. What's actually complicated is separating the free options that hold up from the free options that quietly become $20/month. That's what this post digs into.

We'll walk through Github Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Why Static Hosting Is Free, and Netlify Free Tier — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Github Pages
paragraphs: The foundation looks like this: GitHub Pages is a free static-hosting service built directly into the repo that already hosts your code.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: Point Pages at any subdirectory of a repository and GitHub serves it over HTTPS with a built-in URL, custom domain support, and automatic deploys on every push. For a static blog the entire hosting bill is zero, with no server, no DNS glue, and no renewal dates.
The links in the sources section go straight to the primary docs.
bullets: Pick a directory (e.g. autopilot-blog/site/) as the site source in repo Settings → Pages
Push (or let the engine push) the built HTML and the site deploys in under a minute
Optionally map a custom domain in the same settings page

source.title: GitHub Docs — About custom domains and GitHub Pages

sections.heading: Cloudflare Pages
paragraphs: Start with the basics. Cloudflare Pages is a free static hosting platform with a global CDN and preview deploys for every pull request.

In practice that means: Connect a Git repo and every branch or PR gets its own preview URL, while the main branch gets a production URL on Cloudflare's network. The free tier covers static sites comfortably and custom domains are supported without a separate CDN bill.
For a personal project or side business, this covers you without breaking a sweat.
bullets: Create a Pages project in the Cloudflare dashboard and link the repo
Point the build output at the static folder
Add a custom domain in the project's domains tab

sections.heading: Why Static Hosting Is Free
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: Static sites are cheap to host because there is no server to keep awake — which is why so many hosts give the tier away.

Concretely: Files are cached at edge nodes and served from memory; there is no database, no runtime, no scaling. When the marginal cost of serving a page approaches zero, hosting becomes a feature to win signups — and that is the deal a personal blog gets to keep.
Write down what you change and why — your future self will thank you.

sections.heading: Netlify Free Tier
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Netlify's free tier hosts a static site with SSL, CI/CD from Git, forms and generous bandwidth — no card required.

Concretely: Netlify is the classic pick for static sites: drag a folder in or connect a repo, and it handles builds, redirects, and TLS certificates automatically. The free plan's limits are far beyond what a personal blog ever needs.
For a personal project or side business, this covers you without breaking a sweat.

faq.question: Can I keep this free forever, or is it a trial?
faq.answer: Netlify's free tier hosts a static site with SSL, CI/CD from Git, forms and generous bandwidth — no card required. Treat that as the working assumption and re-check the docs once a quarter.

faq.question: What are the real limitations of free hosting for static website?
faq.answer: The honest answer: Netlify's free tier hosts a static site with SSL, CI/CD from Git, forms and generous bandwidth — no card required. Keyless public endpoints can get throttled if you hammer them, so batch your requests and cache what you fetch.
